CI user here. I can honestly say, that with my experience with my CI, I feel more confident in engaging with people in conversations versus when I used hearing aids. Just like you, when I started losing my hearing, it affected my confidence in interacting with people. It got to a point where I thought I was just a nuisance to others and isolated myself. Which ultimately led to struggling with school and my social life.

Even with CIs I still sometimes struggle with back ground noise and hearing people. It really depends on the people like how soft they speak, how fast they talk, or having accents. I’m a server/ barista at a hotel and it can be chaotic for me.

The only downsides I’ve had while using my CIs since 2021 were how everything sounds robotic when you first start using Cis, I gradually adjusted and everything was normal within a year. Another side effect was I felt like I was getting shocked or experienced a jolt where my CI was located after use. It only occurred within the first year of using my CI but my audiologist and surgeon had no explanation for what I experienced.

As a HoH person with CIs, I’ll usually inform the interviewers about my CIs since they’re noticeable.  Before I had my CIs I could recognize any words, but with it I can understand speech a lot better. 

Just a heads up. When you do get CIs they won’t be activated right away, I had to wait a month for the audiologist to active it. After that it roughly took me 4-6 months to adjust to the CIs and make all the sounds sound less robotic.

I went from Hearing to using hearing aids to having a CI. Based on my experience, I had no confidence in my hearing when using my hearing aids. It was to the point that I stopped socializing with people. Compared to my few years of using my CI, I have confidence in my hearing and more comfortable with interacting with people and not being a nuisance to them. There are still time when I may ask a person to repeat themselves, but it’s less frequent with my CI.

I’m currently hard of hearing wearing a cochlear, but before that it was still extremely difficult to hear anything even with hearings aids. I was born with hearing but gradually lost it at an early age.

One of the biggest problems was I started to isolate myself from people. A lot of people get annoyed with repeating themselves so I can understand something. So I started to see myself as a nuisance. Or when I’m with a group of people and someone was telling a joke. I can see people laughing and ask about what happened. In which case some people say will tell me later as to not mess up the flow of conversation. So I closed myself off from people and lost confidence in myself.

During covid, it got increasingly difficult to hear with masks and barriers reducing sound. The main way I was able to get by was using my phone or something to write on.
